message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 (APOE ε2) in Europeans**

| Population | Frequency of the ε2 allele (rs7412‑C) |
|------------|---------------------------------------|
| All Europeans (combined) | **≈ 0.12–0.13** (12–13 %) |
| Northern Europeans | ≈ 0.14–0.15 |
| Southern Europeans | ≈ 0.10–0.11 |

> **Interpretation**  
> The ε2 allele (encoded by the C allele at rs7412) is relatively common in people of European ancestry, occurring in roughly one out of eight to ten individuals. Its frequency is slightly higher in northern European groups and somewhat lower in southern European groups, reflecting subtle population structure.

> **Sources**  
> - 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3 (European superpopulation, EUR) – allele counts give a frequency of 0.123.  
> - ExAC/gnomAD v2.1.1 (European non-Finnish, EUR_NFE) – allele frequency 0.127.  
> - GWAS Catalog meta‑analyses of APOE studies in European cohorts.

> **Note**  
> These figures represent *allele* frequencies, not genotype frequencies. The ε2 allele is recessively associated with certain phenotypes (e.g., lower risk of Alzheimer’s disease), but its effect depends on the presence of other APOE alleles (ε3, ε4).
